cards.title: Equities: Treasury Presses the Fed as Oil Risk Persists
cards.body: The S&P 500 trades at {SPX} and the Nasdaq 100 at {NDX}. On 13 November Treasury Secretary Bessent urged the Federal Reserve not to raise rates into what he called an energy supply shock from the Iran war. Oil, at {BRENT} for Brent, remains the main channel to equities: Iran's Guard claims new mine hits around Hormuz and fired drones at Bahrain, while the US pause in strikes on Iran has held since 7 November. Nvidia's chief executive resigned on 12 November after admitting an affair with a woman accused of spying for China; the board gave no reason. Trump is due to meet Xi in Shenzhen next week.

cards.title: Oil: Gulf Exports Recover as Hormuz Attacks Mount
cards.body: Brent trades at {BRENT}. Kpler said on 24 November that Gulf producers other than Iran exported just under 14 million barrels a day in September and October, about their pre-war level, with Saudi Arabia and the UAE above it. The risk sits on the ships: about 10 tankers have been reported struck near Hormuz since 16 November, the IMO counts 25 seafarers dead, and insurer The Swedish Club advises avoiding the strait. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.

cards.title: Crypto: FBI Says North Korea Stole $400 Million With Fake Video Calls
cards.body: Bitcoin trades at {BTC}. The FBI said this week that North Korean state hackers took more than $400 million in cryptocurrency from over 900 victims using fake video calls, and that the regime relies on such theft to fund its weapons program (BBC). That is a direct pathway from crypto theft to a sanctioned state's weapons funding. On 6 November the US Treasury sanctioned eight Canadian money-exchange businesses it says moved Iranian funds, including the crypto firm Cryptoyal. OFAC's list of recent actions for 10-15 November shows no designation tied to the $6.3 billion Binance theft the FBI attributes to North Korea.

cards.title: Gold: No War-Linked Driver Found
cards.body: Gold trades at {GOLD}. This run's research found no report tying gold's move to the war in the 12-15 November window. The card's last dated check is from 18 September, when gold was $4,364.46 an ounce at 9 a.m. New York time (CNBC), flat while Brent swung. Inference, not a sourced finding: gold appears to be tracking real yields and the cost of holding it rather than escalation risk.
